elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 (retained, untouched): "Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents ... and defend and save each of them harmless" — an express defend obligation running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2: indemnity "from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees"; "Third Party Claims" is defined in 11.1 as suits, investigations, claims or demands of Third Parties, and "AbbVie Indemnitees" expressly includes Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence in 11.2: "(a) any allegation that the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents or Harpoon Know-How infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right of a Third Party" — the deal-appropriate analogue of Services/Deliverables in this development and option agreement; drafted as "[w]ithout limiting the foregoing ... include", so it supplements rather than contradicts the redacted trigger list.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Inserted 11.2 limb "(b) Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law"; "Applicable Law" is a defined term used elsewhere in the Agreement, so no undefined trigger is created.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Inserted 11.2 limb "(c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of AbbVie's Confidential Information or data caused by Harpoon" — Vendor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure of Customer data.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Inserted 11.2 limb "(d) Harpoon's gross negligence or willful misconduct" — both categories expressly captured.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 11.3 (retained): "The Indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice (an \"Indemnification Claim Notice\") of any Losses ... upon which such Indemnified Party intends to base a request for indemnification under this Article 11", with a favourable no-prejudice-for-delay proviso left intact.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4.1 (retained): "at its option, the indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim by giving written notice to the Indemnified Party within [***]", subject to Sections 7.4/7.5/7.6 — control is expressly allocated.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4.4 (retained): the Indemnified Party "shall ... cooperate in the defense or prosecution thereof and shall furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested", with expense reimbursement preserved.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence in 11.1: "AbbVie's indemnification and defense obligations under this Section 11.1 are limited to Third Party Claims arising from or occurring as a result of (a) materials, Information or content provided by AbbVie or its Affiliates hereunder and (b) AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law." The "limited to" formulation caps the redacted trigger list rather than leaving it open, so the two sentences read consistently.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted 11.2 limb (a) covering allegations that the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents or Harpoon Know-How infringe or misappropriate Third Party intellectual property.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the condition does not apply because no Customer-modification carve-out was added and none is required; the absence is Customer-favourable and leaves the indemnity broader than the fallback contemplates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion is present, which is Customer-favourable and does not defeat the checklist item.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion is present, again Customer-favourable.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in Article 11 or the inserted language; to reach the fallback the drafter would have to add an express Harpoon obligation to procure the right to continue use, modify or replace the infringing item.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop is present; the operative text contains no refund mechanic tied to unavailability of the procure/modify/replace remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Article 11 contains no 3x-annual-fees super-cap. Mechanically unmet, though the absence of any cap on Harpoon's indemnity is Customer-favourable and should not be volunteered.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Duplicate check confirms no cap language, formula or cross-reference to a liability cap was inserted in the redline.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the rendered record: the four architectural elements (defend duty to AbbVie and Affiliates, third-party claim indemnity, notice in 11.3, control of defence in 11.4.1, cooperation in 11.4.4) are already met and untouched, and the two insertions supply the four missing scope limbs (IP infringement/misappropriation, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access or disclosure of Customer Confidential Information or data, gross negligence or willful misconduct) plus the narrowing of AbbVie's own 11.1 indemnity.

The 11.2 insertion is drafted as "[w]ithout limiting the foregoing ... include", so it is additive to the redacted trigger list and cannot contradict it; the 11.1 insertion uses "are limited to", which caps rather than conflicts with the redacted list. Neither creates a dangling cross-reference or undefined term (Applicable Law, Information, Licensed Compounds/Products, Harpoon Patents/Know-How are all defined).

Intent is preserved: the 11.3/11.4 procedural mechanics, the no-prejudice-for-late-notice proviso, expense reimbursement and the "[s]ubject to Sections 7.4, 7.5 and 7.6" priority all survive unchanged, and Section 7.4 is itself expressed to be subject to Section 11.2, so the patent-defence allocation and the indemnity read together without contradiction.

Minimality holds: nothing existing is deleted, the additions map one-to-one onto checklist elements 3-6 and 10, no survival tail, expense, damages-category or procedural boilerplate is added, and the 11.3/11.4 procedure is not duplicated.

Fallback level is not complete and should not be relied on: there is no procure/modify/replace remedy and no refund of applicable fees where those remedies are unavailable, and no 3x-annual-fees super-cap. If the counterparty resists the preferred insertions, the drafter must add an express remedies ladder (procure continued use / modify / replace, failing which refund) before the fallback can be claimed; the absent super-cap is Customer-favourable and should not be offered unprompted.

Note for the drafter: the scope ask is contingent on redacted triggers. If the unredacted 11.1/11.2 lists already carry this scope, operations 1 and 2 should be withdrawn to avoid duplicative operative language; the margin comment already frames this as a scope-confirmation request, which is the right posture.
